title: Write a value as a text block

blocks.text: A text block needs far fewer escapes than a traditional literal, but not none. The page lists what is left: a backslash is still an escape character, **three quotes in a row** would close the block, **trailing spaces** are stripped unless fenced with `\s`, and **a quote just before the closing delimiter** would run into it.
Write `TextBlockSource.of(String value)`. It returns Java source for a text block whose value is `value` (which holds no `\r` and no tab):

items: each line of `value` (split on `\n`), indented by eight spaces, followed by `\n`, except that an empty line other than the last is written with no indentation at all;
the closing `"""` right after the last line, so a value ending in `\n` ends with an empty last line: the closing delimiter on its own line.

blocks.text: Inside a line, escape only what must be escaped:

items: in each run of consecutive `"`, every third quote is written `\"`, so `"""` is written `""\"`;
if the line ends with a space, that last space is written `\s`;
on the last line, if the value's final character is a `"` not already written `\"`, it is written `\"`.

cases.says: Lines are written under the opening delimiter, indented eight spaces, and single double quotes need no escape.
A backslash is still an escape character in a text block, so it is written \\.
Three quotes in a row would close the block, so every third quote of a run is written \".
A line that ends with spaces writes its last space as \s, so the compiler keeps them all.
A value whose last character is a quote writes that quote as \", so it does not merge with the closing delimiter.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A backslash is still an escape character, so paths and regexes double it as in a traditional literal.
A quote right before the closing delimiter must be escaped so it does not merge with it.
Single and double quotes need no escape in a text block.
Three consecutive quotes inside a text block need at least one of them escaped.
